# Configure multiple listeners

You can define the `listener` stanza more than once in a Boundary configuration file to make a controller or worker respond on multiple addresses. Each stanza configures one address and one purpose.

## Requirements

- A controller requires at least one listener with the `api` purpose and exactly one listener with the `cluster` purpose.
- To serve the same purpose on two addresses, define two stanzas with the same `purpose` value — except `cluster`, which allows only one stanza.

## Listen on localhost and a private interface

The following example makes a controller serve the API on localhost and accept cluster connections from workers on a private interface.

1. Open the Boundary configuration file.
1. Define one `tcp` listener stanza for each address.

   ```hcl
   listener "tcp" {
     purpose = "api"
     address = "127.0.0.1:9200"
   }

   listener "tcp" {
     purpose = "cluster"
     address = "10.0.0.5:9201"
   }
   ```

1. Restart Boundary.

If you omit `address`, Boundary binds a TCP listener to the default address for its purpose. Refer to [Listeners](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners#listener-purposes) for the default addresses.

## Listen on Unix domain sockets

To use Unix domain sockets instead of TCP, set the listener label to `unix` and set `address` to a filesystem path.

```hcl
listener "unix" {
  purpose = "api"
  address = "/var/run/boundary-api.sock"
}

listener "unix" {
  purpose = "cluster"
  address = "/var/run/boundary-cluster.sock"
}
```

You can mix TCP and Unix listeners in the same configuration file.
